page.summary: Turn manually hit basic Great repair checks into progress on a worthwhile generator; release the engine when checks, pressure or target value do not support it.

verdict.recommendation: Try the current manual Hyperfocus route only if you can hit compatible Great checks consistently. The former Stake Out automation is not the current engine, and the post-10.2 evaluation is provisional.
verdict.soloQ: Choose a useful repair target before investing in the check chain; do not leave an urgent rescue uncovered to defend your stack.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call the repair target and rescue coverage, but treat execution as your own check-timing task rather than a guaranteed team bonus.
verdict.mainWeakness: A Good check, failed check or any interruption removes Hyperfocus tokens; skill demand and target changes can erase the expected payoff.

options.whyItsHere: Manually hit consecutive Great repair checks to build up to six tokens; a Good, miss or interrupted action resets the chain.
See the closest grouped trio of generators and gain 4/5/6% repair speed on those highlighted targets; choose one only when its completion matters.

item.name: Toolbox
item.why: The snapshot makes a Toolbox optional. Spend charges only when they help finish a valuable target; no add-on package or special-check interaction is established.

opening: Choose a generator whose completion changes the team's rotation. A highlighted Déjà Vu target is a candidate, not an order to ignore a nearer rescue or safer repair.

rows.situation: A valuable generator is reachable and repair time is available.
rows.action: Commit to that target while it is safe; if the team needs a rescue or the Killer contests it, change jobs instead of guarding a potential check chain.
rows.why: Progress only matters if the selected generator remains worth the time.

rows.situation: You are repairing and receive compatible basic Skill Checks.
rows.action: Aim for genuine Great checks to build Hyperfocus. Expect up to six tokens, with each token raising check odds and pointer speed by 4% and the Great bonus by 10/20/30% of its base value by tier. Reassess after a Good, failure or interruption resets all tokens.
rows.why: The current route rewards manual accuracy; special-check conversion does not replace the basic-check execution requirement.

rows.situation: One of Déjà Vu's closest grouped trio is a useful current target.
rows.action: Use its aura and 4/5/6% repair bonus while the target is still strategically valuable; leave if the highlighted group updates or the target loses priority.
rows.why: The highlighted trio is information and a speed opportunity, not a fixed assignment.

rows.situation: The selected generator can be completed sooner with remaining Toolbox charges.
rows.action: Spend charges for the concrete finish, then return to ordinary repair or rescue when the charge spend no longer changes the outcome.
rows.why: The item is optional and finite; it does not recreate the obsolete automated check engine.

abortWhen: Stop protecting a lost check chain when pressure interrupts repair, or when a rescue or better generator is now the higher-value job.

strengths: Manual Great-check accuracy can add repair progress without relying on the old converted-check interaction.
weaknesses: Mechanical consistency is required; interruption or a non-Great check clears the Hyperfocus chain.
commonMistakes: Assuming Stake Out's former automated special-check route still powers Hyperfocus.
Keeping a poor generator assignment merely to preserve or rebuild tokens.
